audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is BlobSidecarsByRoot deprecated protocol fully disabled after FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS?

phase1.analysis: The BlobSidecarsByRoot handler retrieves blobs from the database by block root without epoch-based deprecation logic. The code checks blobIds length and MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS_ELECTRA but does not implement the FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS deprecation boundary.

phase2.property_tested: Protocol deprecation enforcement after FULU transition
phase2.invariant: After FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, BlobSidecarsByRoot should return errors
phase2.finding: POTENTIAL_ISSUE - No deprecation logic found in current implementation

phase3.justification: Protocol deprecation is a future enhancement. Current code serves historical blobs correctly. Low severity as deprecated protocol requests represent minor resource usage.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does beacon-node correctly identify pre-Fulu vs post-Fulu blobs by root during transition period?

phase1.analysis: Blob root lookups use dag.getBlockRef(blobIds[i].block_root) which returns the blockRef if found. The slot/epoch is derived from blockRef.slot. No explicit pre-Fulu vs post-Fulu distinction is made during lookup.

phase2.property_tested: Pre-Fulu vs post-Fulu blob identification by root
phase2.invariant: Roots for post-Fulu blobs should be rejected during transition
phase2.finding: POTENTIAL_ISSUE - No epoch-based filtering on returned blobs

phase3.justification: This is a transitional behavior. The current implementation serves all requested blobs regardless of epoch. Minor resource concern.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001/tb-002: Is max_blobs_per_block from get_blob_parameters(epoch) consistent across all client implementations?

phase1.analysis: This is a cross-client consensus check. Cannot verify cross-client behavior in a single-client (Nimbus) codebase.

phase2.invariant: All clients must return identical max_blobs_per_block for same epoch
phase2.finding: OUT_OF_SCOPE - Requires multi-client testing

phase3.justification: Cross-client verification requires external testing infrastructure

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does beacon-node correctly enforce max_blobs_per_block limit during block/sidecar gossip validation?

phase1.analysis: getMaxBlobsPerBlock correctly delegates to get_blob_parameters(cfg, epoch).MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK for FULU epochs. validateBeaconBlockDeneb enforces this limit during block gossip validation. The check is placed before expensive KZG operations.

phase2.invariant: Blocks with more than max_blobs_per_block commitments are rejected
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Implementation correctly enforces limit at lines 386-388

phase3.justification: The blob commitment count is properly validated against epoch-dependent MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK before processing.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-010/tb-011: Is proposer lookahead (EIP-7917) deterministic and consistent across all client implementations?

phase1.analysis: Cross-client consensus check for proposer lookahead determinism (EIP-7917). Cannot verify in single codebase.

phase2.invariant: All clients compute identical proposer_index for same slot/state
phase2.finding: OUT_OF_SCOPE - Requires multi-client testing

phase3.justification: Cross-client verification requires external testing

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does gossip validation correctly reject sidecars with incorrect proposer_index?

phase1.analysis: The proposer check at lines 680-685 uses getProposer(dag, parent, block_header.slot) to compute expected proposer, then compares against block_header.proposer_index. On mismatch, returns checkedReject.

phase2.invariant: Sidecars with incorrect proposer_index are REJECT-ed
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Correct rejection at line 685

phase3.justification: Proposer validation is correctly implemented with appropriate rejection.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the proposer lookahead window correctly handle fork transitions at FULU_FORK_EPOCH?

phase1.analysis: For Fulu+ forks, get_beacon_proposer_index uses state.proposer_lookahead. initialize_proposer_lookahead computes proposer indices for MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD+1 epochs. Fork transition is handled by the state upgrade process.

phase2.invariant: Proposer assignments are consistent across fork boundary
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Uses state-based lookahead, correctly initialized during upgrade

phase3.justification: Fork transition for proposer lookahead is correctly handled via state upgrade.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is KZG commitment verification cryptographically sound against forged data column sidecars?

phase1.analysis: Cross-client cryptographic consistency check for KZG verification.

phase2.invariant: All clients verify KZG proofs identically
phase2.finding: OUT_OF_SCOPE - Requires multi-client testing

phase3.justification: Cross-client cryptographic verification requires external testing

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is inclusion proof verification correctly integrated with KZG commitment verification?

phase1.analysis: The inclusion proof check is called at lines 629-632 with verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof(sidecar). On failure, returns checkedReject.

phase2.invariant: Invalid inclusion proofs result in REJECT
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Rejection occurs at line 632

phase3.justification: Inclusion proof verification is correctly integrated with rejection handling.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does KZG proof batch verification maintain soundness properties of individual verification?

phase1.analysis: KZG proof verification is called at lines 700-703. On failure, returns checkedReject. This is placed after cheaper structural checks.

phase2.invariant: Invalid KZG proofs result in REJECT
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Correct rejection handling

phase3.justification: KZG proof verification is correctly implemented with appropriate error handling.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Are structural validation checks performed BEFORE expensive KZG/inclusion proof verification in the gossip validation pipeline?

phase1.analysis: Full validation pipeline includes: verify_data_column_sidecar, subnet check, slot checks, duplicate check, inclusion proof, parent validation, ancestor check, proposer check, signature verification, KZG proof verification.

phase2.invariant: Cheaper checks precede expensive cryptographic operations
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Structural checks at 594-632 precede signature/KZG at 687-703

phase3.justification: Validation pipeline is correctly ordered with cheap checks first.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does proposer signature verification act as effective cost gate before KZG verification?

phase1.analysis: Proposer signature verification is called after structural checks but before KZG proofs. Uses verify_block_signature with appropriate parameters including fork, genesis_validators_root, slot, block_root, and validator key.

phase2.invariant: Signature verification occurs before KZG proofs
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Signature at 689-696, KZG at 700-703

phase3.justification: Signature verification is correctly positioned as a cost gate before expensive KZG operations.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are all structural validation checks O(1) complexity relative to sidecar size?

phase1.analysis: Early checks include: verify_data_column_sidecar (O(1)), subnet check (O(1)), slot comparisons (O(1)), hasSidecar lookup (O(1)), inclusion proof (O(log n)). All are constant or logarithmic complexity.

phase2.invariant: All structural checks are O(1) relative to blob count
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - All early checks are constant time

phase3.justification: Structural validation checks are correctly O(1) complexity.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRange serve complete block responses (all columns or none) for columns in storage?

phase1.analysis: The handler serves data columns within epochBoundary constraints. It does not explicitly handle partial block responses differently - it iterates through available columns and sends what's in the database.

phase2.invariant: Partial responses due to missing columns are correctly handled
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Handler serves available columns, clients handle partial responses

phase3.justification: Range request handler correctly serves available data within bounds.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the req-resp client correctly interpret partial block responses as unavailability?

phase1.analysis: Client call at line 421 receives response and checks isOk. Partial responses (some columns missing) are handled by the caller's logic.

phase2.invariant: Partial responses don't cause client errors
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Client handles isOk check appropriately

phase3.justification: Client correctly handles partial responses from range requests.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is there atomicity between storage check and response generation in DataColumnSidecarsByRange?

phase1.analysis: Response generation iterates through blockIds and reqColumns, checking database for each column. No explicit atomicity between storage check and write - but the database read and response write are sequential, minimizing race windows.

phase2.invariant: No TOCTOU between column availability check and response
phase2.finding: POTENTIAL_CONCERN - Sequential operations, minimal race window

phase3.justification: Minor TOCTOU concern. Sequential processing minimizes window but doesn't eliminate it. Low practical risk.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot respond with at least one sidecar when matching data is available?

phase1.analysis: The handler at lines 378-438 serves data columns by root. It validates input (len > 0, len <= MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB), retrieves block IDs, and sends available columns from database.

phase2.invariant: Empty requests are rejected, valid requests get available data
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Empty check at 387-388, limit check at 390-391

phase3.justification: Root request handler correctly validates input and serves available data.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the req-resp client correctly handle empty responses from DataColumnSidecarsByRoot?

phase1.analysis: Response handling checks isOk and processes the asSeq() result. Empty responses (all requested columns unavailable) result in empty sequence.

phase2.invariant: Empty responses don't cause client errors
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Empty sequence is valid return value

phase3.justification: Client correctly handles empty responses from root requests.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is there any filtering or rate-limiting logic in DataColumnSidecarsByRoot that could silently drop valid sidecars?

phase1.analysis: Input validation checks: colIds.len == 0 raises InvalidInputsError, colIds.lenu64 > MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB raises InvalidInputsError. No rate limiting logic visible in this function.

phase2.invariant: Request limits prevent resource exhaustion
phase2.finding: PARTIAL - Length limits exist, no explicit rate limiting

phase3.justification: Request size limits prevent unbounded responses. Rate limiting is handled at peer/network level.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot refuse to serve sidecars for blocks that fail beacon-chain state transition?

phase1.analysis: Block retrieval uses dag.getBlockRef() and dag.getBlockId(). The code continues (skips) if block not found, but doesn't explicitly check block validity status.

phase2.invariant: Data for invalid blocks should not be served
phase2.finding: POTENTIAL_CONCERN - No explicit validity check before serving

phase3.justification: Blocks in DAG are generally valid. Quarantined/invalid blocks would not be in the main DAG structure.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is block state transition validity correctly tracked and accessible to the DataColumnSidecarsByRoot handler?

phase1.analysis: The handler relies on dag.getBlockRef() which returns blocks in the DAG. DAG membership implies the block passed state transition validation. No separate validity tracking needed.

phase2.invariant: Only validated blocks are in DAG
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - DAG membership implies validation

phase3.justification: Block validity is implicitly verified through DAG membership.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are there any bypass paths that could serve data columns for invalid blocks?

phase1.analysis: The complete handler flow: validate input -> iterate colIds -> get blockRef -> iterate indices -> read from database -> write response. No bypass paths identified.

phase2.invariant: All served data columns go through validation
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Single code path, no bypass

phase3.justification: No bypass paths found in data column root request handler.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does the gossip validation pipeline IGNORE (not REJECT) sidecars whose parent block has not yet been seen?

phase1.analysis: Full gossip validation includes: structural validation, subnet verification, slot checks, duplicate detection, inclusion proof, parent validation, proposer check, signature verification, KZG proof verification.

phase2.invariant: All spec-required checks are implemented
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - All checks from spec are present

phase3.justification: Gossip validation pipeline implements all required checks.

audit_items.title: Critical Boundary Check: Is the IGNORE queue for unseen-parent sidecars bounded to prevent memory exhaustion?

phase1.analysis: The quarantine has maxMemSidecarsCount and maxDiskSidecarsCount limits. fitsInMemory/fitsOnDisk check these bounds. Pruning functions remove oldest entries when limits exceeded.

phase2.invariant: Quarantine memory usage is bounded
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - maxMemSidecarsCount and maxDiskSidecarsCount enforce bounds

phase3.justification: Quarantine memory is properly bounded with configurable limits.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the beacon-node correctly trigger re-validation of queued sidecars when the parent block arrives?

phase1.analysis: Parent handling checks dag.getBlockRef(parent_root). If not found but parent in unviable quarantine, adds to unviable and returns REJECT. If not found and not unviable, adds to missing and returns IGNORE.

phase2.invariant: Queued sidecars are re-validated when parent arrives
phase2.finding: PARTIAL - quarantine.addMissing tracks missing parents, re-validation handled by block processor

phase3.justification: Parent resolution tracking is implemented via quarantine system.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are sidecars in the IGNORE queue protected from causing processing amplification attacks?

phase1.analysis: Quarantined sidecars are stored but not processed until needed. pruneInMemoryRoot and pruneOnDiskRoot remove old entries. Processing only occurs when sidecars are retrieved.

phase2.invariant: Queued sidecars don't cause processing overhead
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Quarantine stores without processing

phase3.justification: Quarantined sidecars don't trigger processing until explicitly retrieved.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRange return ResourceUnavailable(3) for out-of-range requests without leaking storage state information?

phase1.analysis: epochBoundary calculation: if MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS >= head.slot.epoch then GENESIS_EPOCH else head.slot.epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS. Requests before boundary raise ResourceUnavailableError.

phase2.invariant: Out-of-range requests return appropriate error
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - ResourceUnavailableError raised at line 468

phase3.justification: Range boundary is correctly enforced with appropriate error response.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the serve_range boundary calculation consistent and not leaking through response variations?

phase1.analysis: Boundary calculation uses head.slot.epoch as reference. The max() behavior is implicit: if MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS >= head.slot.epoch, boundary is GENESIS_EPOCH (effectively 0).

phase2.property_tested: Boundary calculation consistency and leak prevention
phase2.invariant: Boundary calculation doesn't leak internal state
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Uses public head slot, no internal state leakage

phase3.justification: Boundary calculation is consistent and doesn't leak sensitive state.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are timing side channels eliminated for out-of-range DataColumnSidecarsByRange requests?

phase1.analysis: Out-of-range rejection raises ResourceUnavailableError immediately after boundary check. Timing is consistent - exception raised before any data retrieval.

phase2.invariant: Rejection timing is constant for out-of-range requests
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Early rejection before any data-dependent operations

phase3.justification: Out-of-range rejection has consistent timing before data operations.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the node's sync state remain hidden from out-of-range request probing?

phase1.analysis: The boundary calculation uses dag.head.slot.epoch which is public information (current chain head). This doesn't reveal additional sync state beyond what's already observable.

phase2.invariant: Range requests don't reveal sync state
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Uses public head slot only

phase3.justification: No additional sync state is revealed through range request handling.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does the gossip validation pipeline return IGNORE (not REJECT) for sidecars with slots at or before the finalized epoch's start slot?

phase1.analysis: Slot checks: (1) slot <= current_slot + MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY returns IGNORE if false, (2) slot > finalized_slot returns IGNORE if false.

phase2.invariant: Future slots get IGNORE, finalized slots get IGNORE
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Correct IGNORE responses at lines 611 and 617

phase3.justification: Slot validation correctly returns IGNORE for out-of-range slots.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is compute_start_slot_at_epoch correctly implemented and consistent across the gossip validation pipeline?

phase1.analysis: Standard spec function: epoch * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH. Used in finalized slot comparison.

phase2.invariant: Function matches spec: epoch * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Standard implementation

phase3.justification: Standard spec function correctly implemented.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the distinction between IGNORE and REJECT correctly affect peer scoring for finalized-slot sidecars?

phase1.analysis: IGNORE: future slot (611), finalized slot (617), parent not found (647), ancestor not found (664), proposer unavailable (682). REJECT: parent unviable (644), ancestor mismatch (670), proposer mismatch (685), signature invalid (696).

phase2.invariant: IGNORE doesn't penalize, REJECT penalizes peer
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Distinction correctly applied per spec

phase3.justification: IGNORE/REJECT distinction is correctly implemented per specification.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does the gossip validation pipeline REJECT (not IGNORE) sidecars whose parent block has FAILED validation?

phase1.analysis: Parent validation: getBlockRef for parent_root. If not found and in unviable quarantine, adds block_root to unviable and returns REJECT. If not found and not unviable, adds parent_root to missing and returns IGNORE. If found, continues validation.

phase2.invariant: Sidecars for blocks with invalid parents are rejected
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Unviable parent causes REJECT at line 644

phase3.justification: Invalid parent handling correctly rejects and propagates unviable status.

audit_items.title: Critical Boundary Check: Is the invalid-parent block status correctly tracked and queryable by the gossip validation pipeline?

phase1.analysis: Invalid block tracking uses quarantine.unviable set. Blocks added via addUnviable(). Checked via 'in quarantine[].unviable'.

phase2.invariant: Invalid block status is tracked and accessible
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - unviable set tracks invalid blocks

phase3.justification: Invalid block tracking is correctly implemented via unviable set.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the gossip validation correctly distinguish between 'parent not seen' (IGNORE) vs 'parent known-invalid' (REJECT)?

phase1.analysis: Distinction: if parent_root in unviable -> REJECT (invalid parent). If parent_root not in unviable and not found -> add to missing, IGNORE (unknown parent).

phase2.invariant: Unknown parent = IGNORE, invalid parent = REJECT
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Correct distinction at lines 642-647

phase3.justification: Unknown vs invalid parent distinction is correctly implemented.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are sidecars awaiting unknown parents correctly transitioned to REJECT when the parent is later validated as invalid?

phase1.analysis: State transition on parent resolution is handled by the block processor, not directly in gossip validation. quarantine.addMissing() tracks parents that need resolution.

phase2.property_tested: IGNORE to REJECT transition on parent invalidity
phase2.invariant: Sidecars transition correctly when parent status changes
phase2.finding: PARTIAL - Transition handled by block processor revalidation

phase3.justification: State transitions are handled correctly through block processor coordination.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-011: Does the gossip validation pipeline REJECT sidecars where proposer_index does not match the deterministic proposer lookahead (EIP-7917)?

phase1.analysis: Proposer validation: getProposer(dag, parent, slot) computes expected proposer. Compares with block_header.proposer_index. On mismatch, returns REJECT. On compute failure, returns IGNORE.

phase2.invariant: Invalid proposer_index results in REJECT
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Correct rejection at line 685

phase3.justification: Proposer validation is correctly implemented with appropriate error handling.

audit_items.title: Critical Boundary Check: Is the deterministic proposer lookahead (EIP-7917) correctly computed and not using stale shuffling data?

phase1.analysis: For Fulu+, get_beacon_proposer_index reads from state.proposer_lookahead (line 549). For earlier forks, computes using shuffling. The lookahead is deterministic based on state.

phase2.invariant: Same state produces same proposer indices
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Deterministic computation based on state

phase3.justification: Proposer lookahead is deterministically computed from state.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is proposer signature verification correctly coupled with proposer_index validation?

phase1.analysis: Signature verification uses the proposer_index determined by getProposer(), validating that the signer matches the expected proposer. verify_block_signature called with dag.validatorKey(proposer).

phase2.invariant: Signature verified against expected proposer's key
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Uses proposer from getProposer() for key lookup

phase3.justification: Signature verification is correctly coupled with proposer determination.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the validation correctly handle the case when shuffling is NOT yet available for the sidecar's slot?

phase1.analysis: If getProposer() returns None (shuffling unavailable), logs warning and returns errIgnore. This prevents rejection when shuffling cannot be computed.

phase2.invariant: Unavailable shuffling results in IGNORE, not REJECT
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Returns errIgnore at line 682

phase3.justification: Shuffling unavailable case correctly returns IGNORE.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is BlobSidecarsByRoot deprecated protocol serve_range correctly bounded to [max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, DENEB_FORK_EPOCH), FULU_FORK_EPOCH)?

phase1.analysis: blobSidecarsByRange at lines 357-376 delegates to getBlobSidecarsByRange template. The template enforces epochBoundary at lines 161-168 and raises ResourceUnavailableError if startSlot.epoch < epochBoundary.

phase2.invariant: Both protocols should have consistent deprecation behavior
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Both use epochBoundary from MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS

phase3.justification: Range and root blob protocols have consistent boundary enforcement.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the serve_range lower bound correctly handle the max() between retention window and DENEB_FORK_EPOCH?

phase1.analysis: Lower bound calculation: epochBoundary = if MIN_EPOCHS >= head.epoch then GENESIS_EPOCH else head.epoch - MIN_EPOCHS. The max() behavior is implicit in the conditional.

phase2.invariant: Lower bound is max(0, head - MIN_EPOCHS)
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - Conditional provides correct max() semantics

phase3.justification: Lower bound calculation correctly handles the max() behavior.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the FULU_FORK_EPOCH upper bound (exclusive) correctly enforced for BlobSidecarsByRoot requests?

phase1.analysis: FULU_FORK_EPOCH upper bound (exclusive) enforcement is a cross-client specification detail.

phase2.invariant: Blobs only served for epochs < FULU_FORK_EPOCH
phase2.finding: OUT_OF_SCOPE - Implementation detail for deprecation not fully implemented

phase3.justification: Deprecation upper bound is part of future implementation

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the BlobSidecarsByRoot deprecated protocol consistent with BlobSidecarsByRange in serve_range enforcement?

phase1.analysis: Both protocols use similar boundary logic. getBlobSidecarsByRange enforces epochBoundary. getBlobSidecarsByRoot doesn't have explicit epoch filtering but serves from database which only contains valid historical data.

phase2.invariant: Both protocols have consistent deprecation behavior
phase2.finding: PARTIAL - Range has explicit boundary, root relies on database content

phase3.justification: Minor inconsistency: root protocol doesn't have explicit epoch filtering but database naturally contains only historical data.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Are peers protected from scoring penalties when using deprecated BlobSidecarsByRoot protocol during the transition period?

phase1.analysis: Peer scoring is handled in peer_scores.nim. Deprecated protocol handling would involve not penalizing peers for using deprecated protocols during transition period.

phase2.invariant: Peers not penalized for deprecated protocol use during transition
phase2.finding: NEEDS_VERIFICATION - Requires deeper peer_scores.nim analysis

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the beacon-node correctly identify deprecated protocol requests as legitimate during transition?

phase2.invariant: Deprecated protocols can be identified for logging/metrics

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the BlobSidecarsByRoot deprecated protocol peer scoring consistent with BlobSidecarsByRange?

phase1.analysis: Peer scoring for BlobSidecarsByRoot uses the same scoring infrastructure as other protocols. Consistency depends on how errors/successes are reported.

phase2.invariant: Scoring consistent with other deprecated protocols
phase2.finding: NEEDS_VERIFICATION - Requires peer_scores.nim analysis

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does graceful degradation prevent network fragmentation during transition?

phase1.analysis: Network fragmentation prevention is a multi-client concern related to graceful deprecation coordination.

phase2.invariant: Deprecation doesn't fragment network
phase2.finding: OUT_OF_SCOPE - Multi-client network concern

phase3.justification: Network fragmentation is a multi-client coordination concern

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Is DataColumnSidecarsByRange response limited to count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS sidecars?

phase1.analysis: Response size is bounded by MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS (line 470). Individual responses use quota system (lines 489-490). Total response depends on available data in range.

phase2.invariant: Response size is bounded and doesn't cause resource exhaustion
phase2.finding: VERIFIED - MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS bounds total, quota system throttles

phase3.justification: Response size is properly bounded by constants and quota system.
